title: Any state machine moved by a hidden table of the letter (cipher = F(state), state += g(letter) mod m, m = 2..60): the plain pair S,T is doubled once and not doubled once
k4_result: Plain-fed device with a one-to-one F: 0 of 59 moduli (m = 2..60) fit, in all three forms (C = F(state) with or without requiring different plain letters to move differently; C = F(state + h(plain))). One-line reason, no modulus needed: plain S,T gives cipher S,S at letters 32-33 but R,V at 23-24, and in these devices a plain pair is doubled always or never. Not constrained: equations alone fit 59/59 (all steps zero); many-to-one F fits 34/34 moduli 27-60; cipher-fed device with hidden tables fits 47/59 (every m from 14 to 60). Known alphabets with only the step table hidden: 0 passes of 26,679,752 settings (666,994 keyword alphabets incl. transposition-mixed x 10 views x 4 feeds; 10 checks plain-fed, 8 cipher-fed).
controls: 200 shuffled K4s. 46 break the doubled-pair rule (23%), so K4 breaking it is not unusual. C = F(state), one-to-one: no modulus fits 127, some modulus fits 19, undecided 54. C = F(state + h(plain)), one-to-one: no modulus fits 55, some fits 105, undecided 40. Cipher-fed one-to-one: none 5, some 181, undecided 14. Many-to-one F (3 shuffles): 34/34 moduli each. Known alphabets (3 shuffles): 0 passes of 20.0M, 13.3M, 13.3M settings judged.
planted: 9/9 (4 devices with random hidden tables found by the solver at their modulus: moore m=26, mealy m=26 and m=29, cipher-fed m=26; 4 known-alphabet drifts, one per feed, the exact alphabet and view named; the doubled-pair rule held on all 1,500 texts from random one-to-one devices incl. Wheatstone clocks with random ring sizes, and failed on 375 of 500 many-to-one devices as it should)
scope_limits: Dead only for PLAIN-fed devices whose F is one-to-one (same cipher letter = same value): the step between successive F-inputs must depend only on the two plain letters. That covers C = F(state) and C = F(state + h(plain)) with any hidden tables and any modulus (the argument holds in any group, the solver only checked Z_m for m = 2..60), and Wheatstone-type clocks with any two ring sizes. NOT covered: a many-to-one F (several values showing the same letter, m > 26), which fits every modulus tried; cipher-fed devices with both tables hidden, which fit every m >= 14 and are undecidable from 24 letters; steps that depend on position or on a key word as well as the letter; steps that depend on more than the last letter. The known-alphabet test covers only keyword alphabets from the dictionary (plain, ~cols, ~keyed) in the five standard layouts, Vigenere/Beaufort, modulus 26. Control counts of 'undecided' are searches that hit the node budget (4 x 100,000 nodes per modulus); K4's own results had no undecided modulus in the one-to-one plain-fed models. The clue pre-filter FLAGs the family (a message-fed key does not explain K5's shared words); it was built anyway because the test is exact and costs minutes.

negative.family: State machine stepped by a hidden table of the plain letter (generalised Wheatstone)
negative.hypothesis: K4 comes from a device whose hidden state moves by a hidden amount g(plain letter) mod m after each letter, with the cipher letter read through a one-to-one hidden table F of the state (or of state + h(plain letter)).
negative.scope: C = F(state) and C = F(state + h(plain)), state += g(plain) mod m, all hidden tables, m = 2..60, F one-to-one; includes Wheatstone clocks with any ring sizes. Also the same devices (plain-fed and cipher-fed) on 666,994 dictionary keyword alphabets x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort with only g hidden (26.7M settings, 8-10 exact checks).
negative.outcome: Dead: plain S,T is doubled at 32-33 (S,S) and not at 23-24 (R,V), impossible for every modulus and table; solver confirms 0 of 59 moduli; known alphabets 0 of 26.7M (controls: 46 of 200 shuffled K4s also break the rule, 0 known-alphabet passes on 3 shuffles; planted 9/9). Many-to-one F and cipher-fed hidden tables are not excluded.

follow_ups: Cipher-fed device with ONE side known: C = F(state + h(P)), state += g(C), with h or F a dictionary alphabet and the other hidden. Hidden on both sides it fits every m >= 14; with one side known the 8 equations may decide it.

Many-to-one F with a physical reason for it: a 27-31 cell inner ring holding the 26 letters plus repeats/blanks at fixed dictionary-alphabet positions. With F known up to a keyword the doubled S,S no longer needs equal states and the device can be tested exactly.
